scope: Triggered Pixel Color and Image Match nodes in the Rust typed Input Mapper, with Ouroboros authoring and existing MCP graph operations.
accepted: Only admitted true trigger pulses request asynchronous observations; Apply validates and caches bounded templates, while Apply and Arm never capture or emit autonomous input.

Pixel Color emits red/green/blue/alpha scalar States and a completion Pulse. Image Match emits matched Hold, accepted-match score (zero on no match), last successful desktop-center Position only on a match, and a completion Pulse on match or no match.
Image templates are deliberately authored shared graph/profile/flow configuration; live frames, queued payloads and committed observation values remain actor-private.

Capture authorization is separate from output authorization and binds actual source origin/ancestry, explicit capture_user, active client/generation/capture grant, exact selected window/PID/lifetime and downstream recipients.
Completion evaluates the current actor state, reserves effects and delivers through saved Mapper owners before committing; duplicate, stale or canceled continuations cannot emit input.

Bounds are eight screen nodes, eight pending reads per actor and 32 per session, at most one outstanding request per actor/node. Excess triggers drop only the new read and increment metadata counters while otherwise-valid original input/effects commit.
The earliest accepted trigger is retained in bounded FIFO order. Queued waits have no age expiry; the five-second capture timeout starts at actual dispatch. There is no real-time delivery guarantee.

One physical Mapper capture worker is separate from the existing GUI/MCP worker. Canceled physical work retains its slot; Apply/Arm remain unavailable until it drains. EOF/disarm/Stop cancel logical work and preserve saved-release cleanup.
Mapper uses bounded raw RGBA capture/analysis without PNG encoding or the MCP image transport budget; existing GUI/MCP PNG behavior remains separately bounded.

Ouroboros controls expose capture-user and ROI parameters, template-copy staging with Update/Undo, ordinary pending/completed/dropped counters and retiring-worker state; MCP uses the existing 24-tool surface.
limits: Only virtual devices, one owned x64 GUI, three MCP processes (at most two active) and two disposable x64 target processes with four owned roots were used.

Native evidence covers real pixel/match reads, private actors, capture permission, gated input and hold release, selected-root invalidation before a later trigger, GUI authoring and normal cleanup. Delayed completion, queued DROP-NEW bursts, delayed EOF, stale-ticket, tombstone, reservation and wider failure cases are fake-provider/source evidence only; no native late-result race, broad stress or application/device matrix is claimed.
No hardware/RustDesk/global pointer input, broad desktop capture, clipboard or vision/LLM provider was used.
Full desktop vision, OCR, LLM nodes, broader Mapper operators, hardware/application breadth, historical GUI-stall P1, full Ultra/UI parity and release readiness remain open.
